html:
Raška, Latin Rascia, was the heartland of the medieval Serbian state, and the name others often used for that state. On the map for 1300 it is the Kingdom of Serbia of the Nemanjić family.

Stefan Nemanja became grand prince of Raška around 1166 and joined the Serbian lands. His son Stefan was crowned king in 1217, and another son, Saint Sava, made the Serbian church independent in 1219. The family built monasteries such as Studenica, painted with fine frescoes.

Around 1300 King Stefan Milutin pushed south into lands of the Byzantine Empire and married a Byzantine princess. Silver mines run by Saxon miners made the kingdom rich. In 1346 Stefan Dušan was crowned emperor, and the kingdom became the Serbian Empire. Its western neighbours included Hum and Bosnia; see also Serbia.
